correctness.rationale: For the revised claim in /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md, rotation commutes with T_f and its constant fixed set and 30-state nonconstant complement are invariant under a bijection, giving the upper bound. A 30-cycle therefore consumes exactly the nonconstant sector. On the six size-five rotation classes it induces a six-cycle, and after six steps the phase on a given class is a power of the rotation by commutation. This power has order 1 or 5, giving period 6 or 30 respectively. The repaired orbit-test justification now explicitly requires the image class to have size five before inferring injectivity on that class. An independent, complete 65,536-table census constructed all 32 images and directly decomposed every accepted permutation. It confirmed 28 profiles, 96 period-30 rules split 32/64 by profile, and 4/16/76 by ANF degree. The degree restriction also follows from balance: each four-bit input appears twice at any coordinate, so a reversible truth table has eight ones and vanishing top ANF coefficient. value.rationale: This is the first diameter admitting nonlinear diagonal-transversal examples in the motivating bipermutive setting, so the five-site family is not an arbitrary sample. Iterating the resulting diagonal permutation asks whether the full nonconstant sector can lie in one orbit, and if so how often and at what degrees. The exact census proves that the rotation bound is attained and identifies the frequencies, including many genuinely nonlinear maximizers and both types of constant-state dynamics. The known reversible-rule count is not part of this value judgment.
